customers.name: E-commerce Director (Fashion and Lifestyle Brand)
customers.description: Owner or e-commerce director of a European direct-to-consumer brand or multi-brand webshop, typically fashion, footwear, sports or lifestyle, running on Shopify, Shopware, Magento or Lightspeed. Category return rates of 28-37% (Returnista benchmark 2026 for footwear, clothing and swimwear) make returns a margin problem the director owns. Buys and renews the returns platform.
careAbout: Contribution margin after returns and return shipping
Keeping revenue when shoppers send items back
A return experience that does not hurt conversion or reviews
Expanding to Germany, Belgium and other EU markets without separate processes
winsThem: Exchanges and store credit that visibly keep revenue in the first months
Live within days on the existing shop platform and carriers
Peer brands in the same category using it
A customer success manager who reviews the numbers regularly
theirFear: Return rates eroding margin faster than growth
A stricter or paid return policy driving shoppers to competitors
Another tool that the warehouse and ERP do not understand
Lock-in to a platform that cannot follow multi-country expansion

customerJourneyStories.name: Replacing manual email returns after a peak season
customerJourneyStories.summary: A fashion brand outgrows email-and-spreadsheet returns and adopts Returnista to keep revenue through exchanges.

stages.narrative: After a peak season the inbox fills with return requests, refunds go out before items arrive, and the finance review shows refunds growing faster than revenue.
The director hears about Returnista from a peer brand, sees it in the Shopify App Store listing for returns and exchanges, and reads the Returnista benchmark report on category return rates.

Compares Returnista with Shopify's native returns, Returnless and Loop on exchanges, carrier support and Dutch/German coverage; checks the Essential and Professional pack prices and whether own carrier contracts can be used.
Goes live with an onboarding specialist within weeks on one storefront, with size exchanges and store credit bonus enabled for clothing only.
Returnista becomes the only way to return; the customer success manager reviews exchange conversion and high-return SKUs every few weeks.
Renews and upgrades to Professional to use own carrier contracts, adds the German storefront and the warranty flow add-on; recommends it to peers in the category.

customerJourneyStories.name: Connecting returns to the warehouse system
customerJourneyStories.summary: An operations lead adopts Returnista's WMS integration and approval gate to stop blind returns.

stages.narrative: Parcels arrive without paperwork, staff search orders by name, and refunds are released for items that never came back.
Discovers that Returnista integrates with the WMS already used (for example Picqer or Monta) through the WMS vendor's integration page.
Checks what data is pushed to the WMS, how inspection results flow back, how restock locations are assigned and how claims with photos are reviewed.
Pilots announced returns and inspection-gated refunds for one product category.
All returns are announced in the WMS; automations assign restock locations and release resolutions after grading.
Stays because the warehouse process now depends on the integration; asks for the warranty flow add-on for electronics and footwear claims.

customerJourneyStories.name: A size swap that keeps the shopper
customerJourneyStories.summary: A shopper uses a merchant's Returnista portal to swap shoes for a larger size.

stages.narrative: New shoes are half a size too small and the shopper wants the right size before the weekend.
Finds the return link in the shipping confirmation email and on the shop's returns page; the portal carries the shop's own branding and domain.
Reads the return window, any fee and the options shown; sees the larger size is in stock and an exchange is free.
Submits a first exchange in a few minutes, receives a label instantly and drops the parcel at the nearest carrier point.
Follows the status emails ('en route', 'delivered'); the replacement ships without contacting the shop.
Next time a return is needed the shopper trusts the process, chooses store credit with a bonus and keeps buying from the shop.

customerJourneyStories.name: Becoming a Returnista integration partner
customerJourneyStories.summary: A fulfilment provider standardises on Returnista integration for its webshop clients.

stages.narrative: Several webshop clients ask the warehouse to read returns from Returnista instead of emailed lists.
Learns of Returnista's partner programme and sees peers (Monta, Picqer) announcing integrations.
Reviews API documentation, webhook events and the data mapping between return requests and warehouse orders.
Builds or activates the integration for two clients and runs both flows in parallel for a month.
Every new client using Returnista is connected by configuration; returns arrive pre-announced.
Stays a listed partner, refers clients to Returnista and co-markets the integration.
